messages:
ana: heads up — saw cross-org rows in Insights while testing the canary rollout for dashboard-prefetcher (T502). I was in org-A and a couple of result rows showed org-B ids. :thinking:

mike: whoa. repro steps? is this on canary only or main too?

ana: repro on canary flag only. steps: enable canary for me, open Insights > Recent runs, noticed 2 rows with orgB names. screenshot attached (not included here).

sara: any request logs/traces? can you paste the prefetch request/response?

ana: grabbing logs now. snippet:```
[INFO] 2026-02-11T11:15:23Z prefetcher GET /internal/prefetch?panel=insights user=ana org=org-A trace=trc-9a2
cache_key=md5:/internal/prefetch:/u/ana/sess-7f
cache_hit=false
rows_returned=10
--- next request (cached) ---
[INFO] 2026-02-11T11:15:24Z prefetcher GET /internal/prefetch?panel=insights user=ana org=org-A trace=trc-9a3
cache_key=md5:/internal/prefetch:/u/ana/sess-7f
cache_hit=true org_header=null
rows_returned=5 (2 rows with org=org-B)
```

mike: org_header=null on cache hit — suspect cache key omits tenant id. quick glance at prefetcher util:```js
function cacheKey(req) {
  return md5(`${req.path}:${req.userId}:${req.sessionId}`) // oops no tenantId
}
```

larry: product perspective — this is bad for canary UX. If a canary instance shares cache and it doesn't namespace by tenant, previews can leak. We need immediate mitigation.

ana: my vote: scale canary down to 0 and invalidate prefetch cache across the canary pool. canary flag is feature/insights-prefetch-canary.

sara: agree. also we should add alert/telemetry for tenant-mismatch hits. quick rule: when cache_hit && org_header != req.org -> metric++ and trace.

mike: I'll open a hotfix PR to include tenant id in key and add a one-line guard in cache read: if (cached.org && cached.org !== req.org) { drop cache; emit metric }

mike: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1790 (hotfix + unit test)

larry: rollout plan? roll forward hotfix on canary first then prod. but we should rollback canary until fix lands.

deploy-bot: @mike requested rollback of canary flag feature/insights-prefetch-canary -> starting toggle to 0 across regions. status: in_progress

ana: thanks. can someone add a postmortem checklist item: "prefetch cache keys must include tenant id" and create an automated test simulating quick org switches?

mike: on it — I'll add integration test and an e2e that flips org header rapidly to catch race-based cache leaks.

sara: telemetry TODO: add telemetry counter `prefetch.tenant_mismatch_count` + alert when >5 in 1m. Also add a trace tag for cache_org vs request_org.

larry: also update rollout UX docs: note that any caching layer used by canary must be tenant-scoped or use isolated cache namespaces.

deploy-bot: canary toggle complete -> success. all instances now at canary=0.

ana: verified locally after rollback — no cross-org rows shown. will smoke test after mike's PR lands. :thumbsup: 

mike: PR merged, will trigger canary re-enable once metrics look clean. moving fix to staging now.

sara: leaving follow-up ticket in backlog: INF-2379 (prefetch: tenant-safe cache keys + telemetry + gating e2e).

larry: thanks team. good catch. make sure customer-impacting comms draft if we surface incident to affected users.

ana: filing a short incident note in #incidents and pinging support.

mike: TL;DR: root cause = prefetch cache key omitted tenant id + cache-read didn't validate cached payload org. fix = include tenant in key + defensive drop on mismatch + telemetry/alerts.

sara: cool. closing this thread once monitors are green.
